ai_investigations.rationale: The workflow uses the standard official GitHub Action 'actions/checkout@v4', which is a widely accepted and ubiquitous practice across GitHub Actions workflows. Although pinning by full commit SHA provides a higher degree of immutability against tag mutation, using major version tags (like '@v4') is standard industry practice and does not represent an active supply chain attack or severe vulnerability by itself.

supporting_evidence.detail: The action referenced is 'actions/checkout', which is maintained directly by GitHub.
The workflow configuration explicitly includes strict permissions blocks, mitigating the blast radius of potential compromises.

contradicting_evidence.detail: Using '@v4' relies on mutable tags rather than immutable commit SHAs, which leaves a theoretical window for tag redirection if the repository were ever compromised.

ai_investigations.recommended_action: Pin GitHub Actions to full immutable commit SHAs (e.g., actions/checkout@b4ffde65f46332ab88eb53be808477a3936bae11) for enhanced supply chain hardening, or utilize automated dependency update tools like Dependabot to manage SHA pinning.

findings.title: Action 'actions/checkout' is not pinned to a commit SHA
findings.subject: actions/checkout@v4
findings.why: Tags can be moved or re-pointed: a compromised upstream changes what your pipeline runs (this is how the tj-actions/changed-files supply-chain compromise spread).
findings.remediation: Pin to the full 40-character commit SHA (keep the tag in a comment): `uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # v4`.
